newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke sees 13 billion dm in revaluation - paper.
newsitem.headline: Welteke sees 13 billion dm in revaluation - paper.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said a revaluation of German central bank currency reserves could raise 13 billion marks ($7.5 billion) in windfall profits, the business daily Handeslblatt reported on Tuesday.

In a report released ahead of publication on Wednesday, Handesblatt quoted Welteke as saying the Bundesbank was considering whether to raise the current book dollar rate of 1.36 marks of reserves to 1.50 or 1.60 marks.
It was not clear from the report whether Welteke had named the sum of 13 billion himself or if Handelsblatt had done the calculation itself.

Earlier on Tuesday, Bonn government sources said the Bundesbank would be willing to revalue its dollar reserves at 1.50 marks or higher after having valued these at 1.3620 marks in last year's balance sheet.
The Bundesbank, following general German business practices, values its currency reserves at historic foreign exchange rate lows.
Handesblatt quoted Welteke as confirming that the Bundesbank was considering revaluing its currency reserves but that this would be finally be decided in spring 1998. ($ = 1.731 German Marks)
